title: 《South of Midnight》前总监：一直担心 Xbox 内部「罗马在燃烧」
content:
South of Midnight director was worried about 'Rome burning'
Business
Console
PC
News
South of Midnight director was 'always worried' about 'Rome burning' at Xbox
South of Midnight's former director says, were he making the call, he would not have funded the game he directed—believing that it was only a matter of time until "Rome burns."
Imran Khan
,
Contributing Editor
November 3, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
via Compulsion
South of Midnight director David Sears says
in an interview with MinnMax
that he would not have funded the game if he were in charge at Xbox. While thankful for the opportunity, Sears believed that there was a time limit until Microsoft "turned off the tap" and cut funding on the project.
"There’s always a night when Rome burns," Sears told MinnMax host Ben Hanson, "and I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."
Sears recalls that, during South of Midnight's development, Xbox leadership had been telling studios like Compulsion that their main goal was to build a portfolio of non-mainstream titles to diversify Xbox's library. While Sears does not name Game Pass as a motivating factor, the timing would coincide with Xbox's push to build a storehouse of games for the service.
The comment is a candid display of a developer stating that the portfolio diversification initiative at Xbox was wobbly and did not have a long-term view.
In an interview with Bloomberg
, Double Fine studio head Tim Schafer danced around a similar comment, but believed that the games the studio was making would have had some kind of audience, and profitability would not have saved them.

Former Xbox COO Helen Chiang pushes back on characterizations of her departure
"They were funding a lot of games," Sears says. "They were also funding a lot of studios that I was like 'Well. Okay. Great, I guess you have infinite money, you do you. I want less. I don’t want to feel the weight of the obligation of a giant budget, or an army of six hundred to be responsible for. I want to make something that isn't going to bankrupt Microsoft or the games division.'"
Sears left Compulsion in 2025, so he was not there
when Microsoft began its divestiture from the studio
earlier this year, but he applauds Microsoft for allowing the studio
to go independent rather than shut it down
. Sears characterizes the modern Microsoft as "more humane" than in the past due to his experiences with the company.
"It’s remarkable and commendable, and the fact they didn’t do what their predecessors might have done," Sears says about Compulsion's former parent company.
South of Midnight won a Game Award for Games for Impact, a Change Award, a D.I.C.E. award, a BAFTA, and a 2025 Peabody Award, which then-incoming CEO Asha Sharma
bragged about on social media
before announcing her plans for
a "reset" initiative at Xbox that cut Compulsion loose
.
When discussing how he would have turned off the tap on South of Midnight himself, Sears answered "It just seems like in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable—so of course, it was going to have a shocking outcome."
